feature: Add a string data type to the existing Math.run mini-language: double-quoted string literals with \" and \n escapes, + overloaded (number+number adds, string+string concatenates, mixed = type error), print of a string emits raw content, and the builtins len(x) and upper(x). All stage-1 numeric behavior is preserved.
accepted_patch_note: This stage's accepted_solution.patch is the COMBINED stage-1 + stage-2 implementation (numeric interpreter PLUS strings), generated against pristine so the staged validator can apply it directly to the pinned clone and pass the stage-2 hidden tests. The real harness seeds this stage with the previous stage's candidate (input_source: previous_candidate); the combined reference patch is the ground-truth equivalent for validation.
implementation: Lexer.cs: scan double-quoted string literals into a String token, unescaping \" -> '"', \n -> newline, \\ -> '\\'; unterminated string or unknown escape raises MlError. Add ',' as a Comma token (for call argument lists).
Ast.cs: add StringLiteral (unescaped content) and Call (callee name + argument list) expression nodes.
Parser.cs: in primary, produce StringLiteral for a String token; when an identifier is immediately followed by '(' parse a Call (comma-separated args, here arity 1), otherwise a VariableRef.
MlValue.cs: widen the union to {Number, String}; add FromString, IsNumber/IsString, TypeName, and make Display() emit the raw string for string values.

Interpreter.cs: StringLiteral -> string value; '+' overloaded (num+num add, str+str concat, otherwise MlError 'cannot add <t> and <t>'); other arithmetic ops and unary minus require numbers (else MlError); Call dispatches len (string -> number length) and upper (string -> uppercased), each arity-1 and string-typed.
stage_integration_points: Strings touch nearly every stage-1 file: Token (String/Comma kinds), Lexer (string scanning + escapes + comma), Ast (StringLiteral + Call nodes), Parser (string primary + call syntax), MlValue (Number|String union + string Display), Interpreter (+ overload, type errors, len/upper, string-aware unary/arithmetic). Only Environment.cs and MlError.cs are unchanged. This cross-cutting threading is the hard-to-bolt-on integration.
key_traps: The + operator can no longer assume both operands are numbers; a naive stage-1 evaluator that reads .Number on every operand will silently mis-handle strings - the value model must become a tagged union and every arithmetic path must branch on kind.
len returns a NUMBER (so len(s) + 1 is arithmetic), while upper returns a STRING; getting the result kinds wrong breaks composition cases.
Escapes are resolved at lex time, so the stored string content already contains the real characters; print emits them raw (a \n becomes a real newline in the joined output).
Mixed number+string '+' must produce the same 'error: <message>' single-line output as other errors, not a thrown/uncaught exception.
baseline_behavior: Seeded from the stage-1 candidate (numeric-only). With no string support, string literals fail to lex/parse and len/upper are unknown, so every string hidden check fails while numeric ones may still pass. Against pristine (validator baseline) Math.run is absent and all checks fail.
expected_failure_summary: Baseline (validator, pristine - feature absent): 0/16 hidden checks pass. Accepted (combined numeric+strings reference applied to pristine): 16/16 pass.
